dsa-stack-trace-07: Yahan do alag operations hain: `pop()` top hatata hai, `peek()` sirf top print karta hai — stack nahi badalta. Answer bottom → top maanga hai.
Har operation ke baad stack bottom → top likho, jaise [A, B]. peek pe value print karo par list same rakho; pop pe rightmost hatao.
push A, push B → [A, B]; peek prints B, stack ab bhi [A, B]. Ab push C aur do pops chalao. Trap: peek ko pop mat samjho.
dsa-stack-trace-08: Value nahi, stack ka sabse bada size poocha hai. Operator aate hi do values nikalti hain aur ek wapas jaati hai — size 1 kam hota hai.
Operand → size + 1, operator → size − 1. Har token ke baad size likho: 8, 2, 5, *, +, 1, 3, 2, *, +, 4, -, /.
Pehle paanch tokens: 1, 2, 3, 2, 1. Ab 1, 3, 2 aate hain — size kahan tak jaata hai? Trap: saare 7 operands ek saath stack pe mat maano.
dsa-stack-trace-09: Teen cheezein decide karti hain: precedence (^ > * > + −), `-` aur `+` left-associative, aur `^` right-associative. Dhyan do dono `^` pe.
Rule: aane wala operator stack ke top ko pop karta hai agar top ki precedence zyada ho, ya barabar ho aur operator left-associative ho. `^` ke liye barabar pe pop nahi.
a → out, `-` → stack, b → out. Ab `+` aaya: `-` barabar precedence, left-assoc → pop. Out `a b -`. Ab c, `*`, d, `^` … continue karo. Trap: doosre `^` pe pehla `^` pop mat karo.
dsa-stack-trace-10: 'Must be true' poocha hai — har valid sequence me sach hona chahiye. Pehle dekho 4 print hone ke waqt stack me kya pada hai.
4 pehle print = 1, 2, 3, 4 push, 4 pop → stack [1, 2, 3], 3 top pe. Stack wali values ulte order me hi niklengi; 5, 6 abhi bhi push ho sakte hain.
Har statement ke liye ek counter-example dhoondo: jaise 4 3 2 1 5 6 ya 4 5 3 2 1 6. Jo kisi ek se toot jaaye wo 'must' nahi. Trap: 'ho sakta hai' ko 'hona hi chahiye' mat padho.
dsa-stack-trace-11: Sequence 3 se shuru hai, to 3 print karte waqt 1 aur 2 stack me hain aur 4, 5 abhi aane baaki hain. Ab sirf baaki chaar ka order gino.
Condition: 2 hamesha 1 se pehle (stack). 4 aur 5 ko beech me kahin bhi push-pop kar sakte ho, par agar 4 aur 5 dono stack me hon to 5 (upar) pehle niklega.
Case 2 pehle nikla: baaki 1 (stack me), 4, 5 — inke valid orders likho (jaise 1 4 5). Phir case 4 pehle, case 5 pehle. Trap: 4! sab orders mat gino.
dsa-stack-trace-12: Function pehli galti ka index return karta hai. String me har bracket type ki ginti barabar hai, par order bhi match hona chahiye.
Opener → push; closer → pop karo aur check karo ki pop hua opener iska jodi hai. `enumerate` index 0 se gin-ta hai.
`{[()()]}` indices 0–7 pe hai aur stack khaali chhodta hai. Ab index 8 `(` aur 9 `[` push karo; agla character kya pop karega? Trap: index 1 se mat gino.
dsa-queue-deque-06: front = 6 aur rear = 3: rear front se chhota hai, matlab queue array ke end se wrap hoke shuru me aa gayi hai.
Count $=(\text{rear}-\text{front}) \bmod 8$. rear next free slot hai, to wo khud count me nahi aata.
$3-6=-3$ negative hai, to mod 8 lo. Ya seedha gino: slots 6, 7, phir 0 se kahan tak? Trap: $|3-6|$ ya slot 3 ko gin lena.
dsa-queue-deque-07: Ek slot hamesha khaali rakha jaata hai taaki full aur empty alag dikhein. Empty ka test pehle yaad karo, full usse alag hoga.
Empty: front == rear. Har enqueue: rear = (rear + 1) % n. Full tab jab ek aur enqueue rear ko front pe pahuncha de.
Chhota case lo: n = 4, front = 0. 3 enqueues ke baad rear = 3. Ab kaunsa option sach hai? Trap: `rear == n - 1` linear queue ka test hai.
dsa-queue-deque-08: Count queue operations ka hai — har enqueue aur dequeue, moves bhi. Ek element Q1 se Q2 le jaana = 1 dequeue + 1 enqueue.
push(x) ka cost = 1 + 2·(Q1 ka size). pop = 1 dequeue. Har step pe Q1 ka size likho.
push(1): 1 op, Q1 size 1. push(2): 1 + 2·1 = 3, size 2. push(3): 1 + 2·2. Ab pop ke baad size kya hai? Trap: move ko 1 op mat gino.
dsa-queue-deque-09: Code ke teen loops hain: pehle k = 4 elements stack me, phir stack se rear pe, phir kuch elements front se rear pe. Teeno chalao.
Stack ulta order deta hai (LIFO). Teesra loop `len(q) - k` baar chalta hai; us waqt len(q) = 6.
Pehla loop: st = [10, 20, 30, 40], q = [50, 60]. Ab `st.pop()` se rear pe daalo — q kya banti hai? Trap: aakhri rotation loop mat chhodo.
dsa-queue-deque-10: Input-restricted: daalna sirf rear pe, nikaalna dono ends se. Impossible wala dhoondna hai — jahan agla value beech me phansa ho.
Har sequence ke liye simulate karo: agla printed value kisi end pe nahi hai to aur insert karo; agar wo andar dabbi hai to impossible.
Option A (4 1 3 2): 4 ke liye deque 1 2 3 4, rear se 4 hatao → 1 2 3. Ab 1 kis end pe hai? Baaki options bhi aise check karo. Trap: input aur output restricted ko mat badlo.
dsa-queue-deque-11: Har round me do values rear pe jaati hain, teesri discard hoti hai. Ye tab tak jab tak ek value na bache — wahi poocha hai.
Queue front → rear likho. Round: 2 baar (front nikaalo, rear pe daalo), phir front discard. Discarded values ki list bhi rakho.
Round 1: 1, 2 rear pe → 3 discard; queue 4, …, 10, 1, 2. Round 2 me kaun discard hota hai? Aage chalao. Trap: last discarded value bachi hui value nahi hai.
dsa-queue-deque-12: FIFO queue = ek end pe daalo, doosre end se nikaalo. Har design me dekho: dono ends O(1) me pahunch me hain, aur order FIFO hai?
Singly list me head hatana O(1), tail ke baad jodna O(1) (tail pointer ho to). Par tail hatane ke liye usse pehle wala node chahiye.
Circular list me `last.next` kaunsa node hai? Use soch ke option C judge karo. Trap: option D me dono O(1) hain, par order LIFO hai.
dsa-linked-list-06: slow ek step, fast do step chalta hai. List me 6 nodes hain (even), to do 'middle' hain — loop kis pe rukta hai, wo trace se dekho.
Har round ke baad (slow, fast) likho. Loop tab tak jab tak `fast` aur `fast.next` dono None na hon.
Start (3, 3). Round 1: (8, 1). Round 2: slow aur fast kahan? Phir check karo fast.next None hai ya nahi. Trap: pehla middle maan ke ruk jaana.
dsa-linked-list-07: Har round me `p.next` ek node aage jump karta hai (beech wala node chhoot jaata hai), phir p naye next pe jaata hai.
Boxes aur arrows banao: 1 → 2 → … → 7. Har round: p ka arrow do aage, phir p ek aage (naye arrow pe).
p = 1: 1.next = 3, p = 3. Ab p = 3 pe yahi karo, aur dekho p 7 pe pahunch ke kya hota hai. Trap: 7 ko gayab mat maano.
dsa-linked-list-08: Even values recursive call se pehle print hoti hain, odd values call ke baad. Pehle wali jaate waqt print, baad wali lautte waqt.
Jaate waqt order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Lautte waqt order ulta: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Even ko pehli list se, odd ko doosri se lo.
Jaate waqt even: 2, 4 print. Ab lautte waqt kaunse odd kis order me aayenge? Trap: odd values ko list order me mat likho.
dsa-linked-list-09: Condition `cur.val < head.val` hai — aur `head` loop ke andar badalta hai. Har baar current head se compare karo, original 5 se nahi.
Chhota node mile: use unlink karo aur head ke aage lagao (naya head), cur = prev.next. Warna prev aur cur ek aage.
head = 5: 8 rukta hai. 2 < 5 → front pe, head = 2. Ab 7 aur 1 ko naye head 2 se compare karo. Trap: 5 se compare karte rehna.
dsa-linked-list-10: Har option me dekho: operation ke liye kaunsa node chahiye, aur kya wo pointer seedha mil jaata hai ya walk karni padti hai?
Last node delete karne ke liye uske pehle wala node chahiye (naya tail). Doubly list me `prev` hai; singly me nahi. Circular list me front = `last.next`.
Option A: `tail.prev` se naya tail turant milta hai. Option B me tail se pehle wala node kaise milega? Baaki do bhi aise judge karo. Trap: tail pointer hone se delete O(1) nahi ho jaata.
dsa-linked-list-11: Steps ki ginti poochi hai, node ki value nahi. Cycle 4 → … → 10 → 4 hai; dono pointers har step me saath chalte hain.
Har step ke baad (slow, fast) node values likho. 10 ke baad agla node 4 hai. Tab tak chalao jab tak dono same na hon.
Step 1: (2, 3), step 2: (3, 5), step 3: (4, 7). Fast 10 ke baad 4 pe wapas aata hai — aage chalao. Trap: meeting node ki value ko steps mat likho.
dsa-linked-list-12: b pehle k = 3 node aage jaata hai, phir a aur b saath chalte hain jab tak b None na ho. Gap 3 ka bana rehta hai.
Gap k ho aur b None pe ruke, to a end se k-th node pe hota hai. List me 9 nodes hain; indices 0–8 likho.
for loop ke baad b index 3 (value 4) pe. Ab b ko None tak kitne moves lagenge? Utne hi a ke. Trap: b ko last node pe rokna (None pe nahi).
dsa-search-06: 20 array me nahi hai, to function 'found' nahi, loop ke end pe (lo, hi) return karega. Loop `lo <= hi` tak chalta hai.
Table banao: lo, hi, mid = (lo + hi) // 2, a[mid]. a[mid] < 20 → lo = mid + 1; a[mid] > 20 → hi = mid − 1.
Row 1: lo = 0, hi = 7, mid = 3, a[3] = 18 < 20 → lo = 4. Ab agli rows chalao jab tak lo > hi na ho. Trap: lo == hi pe ruk jaana.
dsa-search-07: Ulta sawaal: comparisons ki limit 6 di hai, sabse bada n dhoondna hai. Worst-case formula ko n ke liye solve karo.
Worst case $=\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$. Condition: $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1 \le 6$, yaani $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor \le 5$.
$\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor \le 5$ ka matlab n, $2^6$ se strictly chhota. Ab sabse bada integer lo. Trap: $n = 2^6$ pe floor 6 ho jaata hai.
dsa-search-08: Key hamesha present hai aur har element barabar likely. Average chahiye — har element ki comparisons jodo aur 15 se divide karo.
15 = $2^4 - 1$: search tree full hai. Depth d pe $2^{d-1}$ keys hain, aur unhe d comparisons lagte hain.
Depth 1: 1 key × 1, depth 2: 2 keys × 2. Depth 3 aur 4 ka bhi jodo, phir 15 se bhaag do. Trap: levels 1–4 ka seedha average nahi.
dsa-search-09: Ye code `lo < hi` aur `hi = len(a)` use karta hai — normal bs se alag. Har statement ko ek chhote array pe trace karke judge karo.
Invariant: a[0..lo−1] sab < x, a[hi..] sab ≥ x. Loop lo == hi pe rukta hai. Equal element pe `hi = mid` hota hai.
Option C test: lo = 0, hi = 1, a[0] < x, aur `lo = mid` ho to mid kya banega, aur lo badlega? Option D ke liye a = [3, 5, 8, 12], x = 8 trace karo.
dsa-search-10: 5 ki copies indices 2–5 pe hain. Ye version jo bhi copy pehle probe ho, wahi return karta hai — leftmost guarantee nahi.
Trace: lo = 0, hi = 15. mid = (lo + hi) // 2; a[mid] > 5 → hi = mid − 1; a[mid] == 5 → return mid.
Pehla probe: mid = 7, a[7] = 11 > 5 → hi = 6. Ab agla mid nikaalo aur a[mid] dekho. Trap: index 1 se mat gino.
dsa-search-11: Positions barabar likely nahi hain: probability i ke proportional hai. Pehle probabilities ko normalise karo (sum 1 hona chahiye).
$P(i) = i / (1 + 2 + \dots + 10) = i/55$. Position i pe key mile to i comparisons. $E = \sum_{i=1}^{10} i \cdot P(i)$.
$E = \frac{1}{55}\sum i^2$. $\sum_{i=1}^{10} i^2 = \frac{10 \cdot 11 \cdot 21}{6}$ — ye nikaalo, phir 55 se divide. Trap: (n + 1)/2 sirf uniform case me.
dsa-search-12: Do absent keys: ek sabse chhoti (search hamesha left), ek sabse badi (hamesha right). Floor mid ki wajah se dono sides barabar nahi ho sakti.
Chhoti key: har probe pe hi = mid − 1. Badi key: har probe pe lo = mid + 1. Har case me probes ki list banao.
Dono ka pehla probe: mid = (0 + 24) // 2 = 12. Left: hi = 11, agla mid = 5. Right: lo = 13, agla mid? Aage chalao. Trap: dono ko worst case 5 maan lena.
dsa-loop-complexity-06: Inner `while` me j = 1 se double hota hai jab tak j < n — ye i pe depend nahi karta. Har i ke liye inner count same hai.
Total = (outer rounds) × (inner rounds). Inner rounds = j ki un values ki ginti jo 20 se chhoti hain: 1, 2, 4, …
j ki values likho: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 — kaunsi < 20 hain? Outer `range(20)` kitni baar? Trap: ⌊log₂ 20⌋ = 4 lena.
dsa-loop-complexity-07: i har baar sirf 1 badhta hai; i² sirf rukne ki condition me hai. Socho: i kahan tak ja sakta hai?
Condition $i^2 \le n$ ⇔ $i \le \sqrt{n}$. Rounds = i ki values 1, 2, 3, … jo is condition ko satisfy karein.
n = 100 lo: i = 1 se kahan tak loop chalega? Phir n = 10000 pe. Count n ke saath kaise badhta hai? Trap: i² dekh ke log n ya n² mat bolo.
dsa-loop-complexity-08: Outer i halve hota hai (64, 32, …), aur inner `range(i, n)` chalta hai — ye n − i baar hai, i baar nahi.
i ki saari values likho jab tak i > 0. Har pass ka inner count = 64 − i. Phir sab jodo.
i = 64 → 0 rounds, i = 32 → 32, i = 16 → 48. Baaki i = 8, 4, 2, 1 ke liye nikaalo aur jodo. Trap: `range(i, n)` ko `range(i)` padhna.
dsa-loop-complexity-09: Yahan i double nahi, square hota hai: i = i · i. Values bahut tez badhti hain — par count n ke saath fir bhi badhta hai.
i ki values $2^1, 2^2, 2^4, 2^8, \dots$ — k rounds ke baad $i = 2^{2^k}$. Rukna jab $2^{2^k} \ge n$.
Dono taraf $\log_2$ lo: $2^k \ge \log_2 n$. Ab k ke liye ek baar aur log lo. Trap: doubling wala Θ(log n) yahan mat lagao.
dsa-loop-complexity-10: Har fragment me inner loop ka count i ke function ke roop me likho. Do nested loops hone se hi n² nahi hota.
`range(a, b, s)` ke values ≈ (b − a)/s. Option B: (i² − 0)/i. Option D me outer i double hota hai.
Option A: `range(i, i + 10)` me kitne values, aur kya wo i pe depend karta hai? Har option ka total sum aise nikaalo. Trap: shape dekh ke judge karna.
dsa-loop-complexity-11: Outer loop step 2 se chalta hai, aur 10 pe rukta hai (10 shaamil nahi). Inner `range(i)` exactly i baar.
Total = Σ i, sirf un i pe jo `range(0, 10, 2)` deta hai.
i ki values likho: 0, 2, … kahan tak? Phir inka sum lo. Trap: 0 se 9 tak saare i jod dena.
dsa-loop-complexity-12: Dhyan do: `j = 0` for loop ke bahar hai. j kabhi reset nahi hota, sirf badhta hai.
Har `c += 1` ke saath `j += 1` hota hai. To total c = j ka total badhna. j maximum kahan tak jaata hai?
n = 4 pe trace: i = 0 → 0 runs, i = 1 → j 0→1 (1 run), i = 2 → j 1→2. Pattern dekho. Trap: maan lena ki har i pe j 0 se shuru hota hai.
dsa-growth-order-06: $f_1 = 2^{\log_2 n}$ dekhne me exponential lagta hai — pehle ise simplify karo. Baaki teen n ki powers (aur ek log) hain.
Identity: $2^{\log_2 n} = n$. Log factor kisi bhi power $n^{\varepsilon}$ se chhota hai, to $\sqrt{n}\log n$ ko n se ratio lekar compare karo.
$\sqrt{n}\log_2 n / n = \log_2 n/\sqrt{n}$ — ye n badhne par kahan jaata hai? Phir $n, n^{1.5}, n^2$ ko exponent se lagao. Trap: $2^{\log_2 n}$ ko exponential maanna.
dsa-growth-order-07: Chaaron bahut bade functions hain; seedha compare mushkil. Har ek ka $\log_2$ lo — order same rahta hai.
$\log_2$: $g_1 \to 100\log_2 n$, $g_4 \to (\log_2 n)^2$, $g_2 \to n\log_2 1.01$, $g_3 \to \log_2 n! = \Theta(n\log n)$. Ab $L = \log_2 n$ ke terms me socho.
$100L$ vs $L^2$: L > 100 hote hi kaun aage? Phir $L^2$ ko $0.0144\,n$ se compare karo. Trap: chhote n pe $1.01^n$ chhota dikhta hai — asymptotic n → ∞ hai.
dsa-growth-order-08: $n_0$ aisa chahiye ki uske baad har n pe $2^n \ge n^3$ ho — sirf pehla n jahan sach ho, wo nahi.
Table banao: n, $2^n$, $n^3$ for n = 1, 2, 3, … Dekho kahan se inequality lagataar sach rehti hai.
n = 1: 2 ≥ 1 sach. n = 2: 4 vs 8 — fail. n = 8: 256 vs 512. Aage n = 9, 10 check karo. Trap: n = 1 pe ruk jaana.
dsa-growth-order-09: Har statement ko rewrite karo: log ka base, $a^{\log_2 n}$ wali power, factorial vs exponential, aur exponent ke andar constant.
Rules: $\log_a n = \log_b n/\log_b a$; $a^{\log_2 n} = n^{\log_2 a}$; $n! \ge (n/2)^{n/2}$; $2^{cn} = (2^c)^n$.
Option B: $4^{\log_2 n} = n^{\log_2 4}$ — power kitni? Option D ke liye f = 2n, g = n leke dekho. Trap: exponent ke andar constant ko ignore karna.
dsa-growth-order-10: Ye Ω wala sawaal hai: $f(n) \ge c\,n^2$ har n ≥ 20 pe chahiye. To c ratio $f(n)/n^2$ ke minimum se zyada nahi ho sakta.
$f(n)/n^2 = 1 - 10/n$. Ye n badhne par badhta hai ya ghatta hai? Minimum range n ≥ 20 ke kis end pe hoga?
$1 - 10/n$ badhta hai, to minimum n = 20 pe. Ab $10/20$ nikaal ke subtract karo. Trap: limit 1 lena — wo bahut bade n pe hi milta hai.
dsa-growth-order-11: Dono functions me n common hai. Usse cancel karo — bacha compare: $\log_2 n$ vs $\sqrt{n}$.
f = O(g) agar f/g bounded rahe; g = O(f) agar g/f bounded rahe. $f/g = \log_2 n/\sqrt{n}$ ka limit dekho.
n = $2^{16}$: $\log_2 n = 16$, $\sqrt{n} = 256$. n = $2^{36}$ pe ratio kya hai? Ratio kidhar ja raha hai? Trap: dono n se shuru hain to Θ maan lena.
dsa-growth-order-12: B ka order bada hai, par A ka constant 64 bada hai. Crossover dhoondna hai — sirf powers of 2 pe check karna hai.
k = 8: 256 vs 512 — nahi. Ab k = 9 aur aage check karo jab tak $2^k$ aage na nikle. Trap: log factor chhod ke $n > 64$ solve karna.
